A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cancer is a 3D chromosomal disease.
the chromatin organization in the nucleus is highly dynamic, and the alterations of 3D architecture are closely linked to transcriptional dysregulations and cancer development.
the 3D chromosomal organization is essential for the regulation of gene expression and its disruption is associated with the development of cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cancer cells reprogram 3D chromosomal organization in a way to facilitate their survival, which is a potential target for therapeutic intervention.
cancer development is a process of chromatin remodeling, which is driven by transcriptional dysregulated enhancers, enhancers–promoters interactions and chromatin topology.
3D chromatins architecture plays an essential role in transcriptional dysregulations and thus cancer progression.
